felt-promotion-empty-squash:
The squash-apply step in `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/promotion-service.ts` lays a worktree branch's owned changes onto a sandbox checked out at `origin/<base>`, stages them, and returns a result of the form `{ conflictedFiles, applied }` — the `applied` boolean tells the caller whether to proceed to the separate commit step.

Requirement: the apply step must return `applied: false` when the apply succeeds cleanly but stages nothing — i.e. the branch's owned paths are all already at their goal state on `origin/<base>`, so the resulting staged index is empty. Today it returns `applied: true` in that case; the caller then runs a git commit against an empty index and fails with "nothing to commit", surfacing a confusing apply error even though nothing went wrong.

Acceptance — the first two are existing behaviour and must not regress; the third is the fix:
1. Branch has owned work not yet on base → applying it stages a non-empty diff → `conflictedFiles` empty, `applied: true`.
2. Applying the owned diff produces merge conflicts → the conflicted paths are surfaced in `conflictedFiles`, `applied: true`.
3. Every owned path already at its goal state on `origin/<base>` → the apply exits clean but stages nothing → `conflictedFiles` empty AND `applied: false`, so the caller skips the commit step. Downstream reconciliation (the existing canary / absorb-paths flow) handles the already-landed paths and is out of scope.

Scope: edit only `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/promotion-service.ts`. Do not change the result shape (conflicted-files list + applied boolean) or the behaviour of the normal and conflicting cases. Do not alter the commit step.
felt-trust-gate-default-on:
The predicate in `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/trust-gate-spawn-gate.ts` reads the environment variable `FELT_FEATURE_TRUST_GATE_SPAWN_BLOCK` and reports whether structural-block semantics are enabled (when enabled, a refused spawn is blocked/aborted; when disabled, it is audited and allowed to proceed). It is currently default-OFF: enabled only when the variable is exactly the string `"1"`. The machinery this flag was gating on has landed, so the safe default is now the opposite — blocking on unless an operator deliberately turns it off.

Flip the predicate to default-ON with a single explicit opt-out. As a pure function of the variable, it must return:
- absent / unset → `true`
- exactly `"1"` → `true`
- exactly `"0"` → `false` (the only disabling value; the emergency opt-out)
- any other value, including `""`, `"true"`, `"yes"`, `"false"`, `"off"` → `true`

In short: invert the sense from "on iff equals 1" to "on unless equals 0".

Scope: a surgical change to the flag-interpretation predicate only, in `trust-gate-spawn-gate.ts`. Keep it a pure function of the env var with no other side effects. Do not alter downstream consumers that take an already-resolved "block enabled" boolean — their behaviour is unchanged and exercised independently.
felt-brief-confusable-areaid:
`createDiskBriefLoader` in `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/brief-loader.ts` validates the set of owned-area ids it is given at construction. An id that resolves to a reserved underscore-prefixed shape must be rejected (throw; the error message must contain `journal-reserved prefix`), because the audit record's envelope `area_id` carries the owned-area scope and a reserved-prefix id would corrupt the audit trail. The single sanctioned exception is the exact literal id `_global`, which must be accepted.

The guard today only inspects whether the raw first codepoint is an ASCII `_`, so an id that an operator reading the roster would perceive as `_…` slips through whenever its literal first codepoint is not an ASCII underscore.

Fix the guard so it rejects any area id that resolves to an underscore-prefixed shape under operator-visible normalisation, while still accepting genuinely non-reserved ids and exactly `_global`. Required outcomes:
- leading zero-width no-break space / BOM, then `_foo` → REJECT
- leading zero-width space, then `_foo` → REJECT
- leading zero-width joiner, then `_foo` → REJECT
- a fullwidth underscore variant, then `foo` (a confusable that normalises to `_foo`) → REJECT
- leading zero-width no-break space / BOM, then the literal `_global` (a confusable of the sanctioned id, not the exact literal) → REJECT
- the exact literal `_global` → ACCEPT (the only reserved id permitted)
- a leading invisible Unicode format character whose remainder does NOT begin with an underscore (e.g. an invisible prefix then `foo`, normalising to plain `foo`) → ACCEPT — do not over-reject
- pre-existing behaviour preserved: a plain ASCII `_`-prefixed id other than `_global` still REJECTs; ordinary unreserved ids still pass

Scope: this is confusable-identifier mitigation for a trusted operator roster — match the enumerated cases, not every conceivable Unicode trick. Edit only `brief-loader.ts`. Do not change the error message text or the construction signature; only the predicate that decides whether an id counts as reserved.
felt-owned-area-confined-read:
`loadOwnedAreaRegistry(rosterDir)` in `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/owned-area-registry.ts` loads a manual roster plus one Markdown Brief per declared area, resolving each Brief by basename inside the roster directory and reading it. On failure it throws a `RegistryLoadError` carrying a `reason` string and (where applicable) an `areaId`; both the `reason` field and the human-readable message are surfaced to callers and matter.

The Brief-read path defends against some hostile/misconfigured directory contents (Briefs are attacker-influenceable in a multi-agent setting) but has two gaps. Close them without regressing the existing checks.

New required cases:
- Brief basename resolves to a **directory** rather than a regular file → reject before interpreting contents, with a `RegistryLoadError` whose `reason` is `schema_invalid` and whose message contains "not a regular file".
- Brief file **exceeds the maximum allowed Brief byte size** (the existing maximum-byte constant for Briefs; the test uses a 257 KB file against a 256 KB cap) → reject on a size basis, before the contents are parsed, with a `RegistryLoadError` whose `reason` is `schema_invalid` and whose message contains "byte cap". This is distinct from any existing line-count cap enforced later by the parser — it must trip on raw byte size.

Existing behaviour that must continue to hold:
- Missing / unreadable Brief → `RegistryLoadError`, `reason` `brief_missing`, `areaId` equal to the offending area's id.
- Symbolic-link Brief (including one pointing outside the roster directory) → `reason` `schema_invalid`, message mentions a symbolic link.
- Brief resolving outside the roster directory → refused as `schema_invalid`.
- Well-formed, in-bounds, regular Brief under the size cap → loads successfully and produces the typed area exactly as before.
- All other registry validations (roster JSON parsing, version checks, regime/activation validation, path validation, area/path caps, duplicate-id and duplicate-basename detection, parent-area chaining and cycle detection, the parser's own line cap) remain unchanged with their existing reasons and messages.

Reason-mapping principle: a genuinely missing or unreadable Brief maps to `brief_missing`; every other rejection arising from the Brief-read step — non-regular file, oversized, symbolic link, path escaping confinement, or any other hostile/misconfigured indication — maps to `schema_invalid`.

Scope: edit only `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/owned-area-registry.ts`.
felt-sync-unchecked-base:
`WorktreeManager` in `src/Felt.AgentService/src/services/worktree-manager.ts` syncs a repo's base branch (e.g. `main`) against its `origin` remote. A repo is laid out as a primary clone plus feature worktrees; the base branch is frequently a ref that the feature worktrees branch from but that is itself checked out in **no** working tree (no checkout has it as live HEAD). Three methods are involved:
- `getSyncPreview(repoName, baseBranch, direction)` → a preview of what a sync would move (commits, changed files, +/- counts) or an `error`.
- `getSyncFileDiffRaw(repoName, baseBranch, direction, filePath)` → the raw diff for one file, or an `error`.
- `syncBaseBranch(repoName, baseBranch, direction, opts)` (`direction` is `'pull'` or `'push'`) → performs the sync; returns `{ success, error? }`.

All three currently bail out as if no base branch existed whenever `baseBranch` is not the live HEAD of some checkout — so the preview returns empty/`error` and `syncBaseBranch` fails, even though the ahead/behind badge (which reads the shared ref store directly) correctly reports the branch is behind. Comparing or advancing a local base ref against `origin/<base>` is a read-only-or-ref-store operation that can run from any checkout of the repo; it does not require the base to be checked out. Fix all three so they operate from any checkout of the repo, erroring only when no clone of the repo exists at all. A test seam (`setMainRepoResolver`) points the repo at a temp clone.

Required behaviour (base checked out nowhere unless stated):
1. `getSyncPreview` for a `pull` where `origin/<base>` is one commit ahead of the local base ref → `error` unset; the commits list contains exactly that one origin-only commit (with its subject); the files list includes the file that commit changed. When the base IS checked out somewhere, prefer that checkout so the preview output is identical to before. Only when no clone of the repo exists at all → error.
2. `getSyncFileDiffRaw` likewise runs from any checkout; it errors only when no clone of the repo exists.
3. `syncBaseBranch(..., 'pull')` when `origin/<base>` is a fast-forward ahead of the local base ref → succeeds; the local base ref is advanced to exactly match `origin/<base>`; NO working tree is modified (whatever branch a checkout is parked on stays on it with its HEAD commit unchanged, and the origin-only files are not materialised into any working tree).
4. `syncBaseBranch(..., 'pull')` when the local base ref has commit(s) origin lacks (non-fast-forward) → fails (`success: false`); the local base ref is left unchanged (no merge commit synthesised, no force-update). The fast-forward-only contract holds on the ref-only path too.
5. `syncBaseBranch(..., 'push')` when the local base ref is ahead of origin → succeeds; `origin/<base>` is updated to the local base ref's tip.
6. When the base IS checked out, behaviour is unchanged — including the existing guard that blocks a pull/push (with a clear error) if that checked-out base has uncommitted changes in its working tree. That dirty-tree guard must apply ONLY when the base is genuinely checked out; an unchecked-out ref move touches no working tree and must not be gated on it. Keep `opts.ffOnly` semantics intact on the checked-out pull path.

Notes: the verifier imports the compiled service module (`worktree-manager.js`) and exercises these methods directly against temporary git repos (a bare origin plus a clone parked on a feature branch, so the base ref is checked out nowhere). The Svelte UI is out of scope. Error wording on the no-clone-at-all path may change — the tests assert on success/failure, ref positions, working-tree state, and preview contents, not on exact error strings.
